definition: A deal whose stage is one of discovery, technical_validation, business_case, or negotiation - i.e. still open, not yet closed_won or closed_lost. Filter with deals.stage NOT IN ('closed_won', 'closed_lost'), not a date-based check.

closed_won deals divided by all closed deals (closed_won + closed_lost) in the filtered set. Never divide by all deals - open deals are neither a win nor a loss and must be excluded from both the numerator and the denominator.

When the question asks for 'average deal size' or 'average deal value' with no other qualifier, use the average deal_value across closed_won deals only. If the question names its own filter instead (e.g. 'average deal value for a specific workload or stage'), use only that filter - do not also add closed_won unless the question asks for it.

The committed spend an account agrees to when a deal closes won (capacity_contracts.committed_amount). This is not the deal value - a deal is the negotiated opportunity; the contract is what gets created from it once won, and consumption_usage tracks draw-down against it over time.

The credits an account has actually used against its capacity contract in a given month (consumption_usage.credits_consumed). Not the same as commitment - an account can be under-consuming (using far less than committed_amount / 12 per month) even while its contract status is still 'active'.

An account whose recent monthly credits_consumed is trending below what capacity_contracts.committed_amount would imply on a straight-line monthly basis (committed_amount / 12). This is the primary renewal-risk signal - derive it from the consumption_usage trend itself, not from capacity_contracts.status alone, since status is a label applied to the account, not a live calculation.

The technical evaluation stage of a deal, tracked in deals.poc_status (not_started, in_progress, passed, failed) independently of deals.stage. A deal can sit in the technical_validation stage with poc_status still in_progress - poc_status is the outcome of that work, not a synonym for the stage.

An account adopting an additional workload beyond the one(s) it already holds an active capacity_contracts for. Candidates are accounts with strong, non-declining consumption in their current workload and no deal yet in a different workload - not accounts with declining usage, which signals risk, not readiness to expand.
A deal where deals.partner_id is not null - a systems integrator, cloud marketplace, or ISV originated or co-sold it. This is a property of the deal, not of the account's general partner history.

Net Revenue Retention - the share of a prior period's committed capacity still retained (renewed or expanded), excluding any new-account revenue. This schema has no single precomputed NRR column; answering an NRR question means comparing capacity_contracts.committed_amount on renewal/expansion contracts against the value they replaced, over a specific period. If the question doesn't name a comparison period, decline in chat mode and ask which one - don't assume a window.
